title: Largest Multiple of Three
summary: Given an array of digits, return the largest number that is divisible by three by rearranging the digits in any order.
statement: Given an array of digits, return the largest number that is divisible by three by rearranging the digits in any order. The result should be returned as a string without leading zeros. If it is not possible to form such a number, return an empty string.
constraints: digits contains one to ten thousand digits from zero through nine.
Choose and rearrange any nonempty subset to make the numerically largest multiple of three.
Return it without leading zeroes; return "0" for all-zero choices and an empty string when impossible.
hints: Divisibility by three depends only on the digit sum.
If the sum remainder is one or two, remove the fewest and smallest digits whose remainders repair it.
Then emit all retained digits from nine down to zero and collapse an all-zero answer.
Maximizing retained digit count dominates; among equal lengths, removing smaller digits maximizes descending lexicographic value.
editorial: Count digits and inspect the total modulo three. Repair remainder one by removing one smallest remainder-one digit or two smallest remainder-two digits; use the symmetric rule for remainder two. Prefer removing one digit whenever possible. The oracle independently enumerates every subset on seeded short inputs and constructs its best descending number.

tests.explanation: All three digits form descending 981, which is divisible by three.
Every arrangement is zero, represented canonically as one zero.
